questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I wanted to experience a completely different culture, far away from home.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: The whole experience was amazing, but i had so many issues with courses and course registration that i overall will rate my exchange 9/10.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Quite easy.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I didn't recieve much information on arrival, but if i had any question, the administration was very helpful.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: On campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
questions.answer: I lived in a dormitory, where we were 6 people sharing one apartment, and 2 people then share one room and one bunk bed.

questions.question: What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
questions.answer: There was a lot of grocery stores and restaurants nearby, so i didn't have any trouble finding food.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living in on campus housing? *
questions.answer: It's a great way to meet plenty of people, and get a lot of new friends. I spend most of my time with the many exchange students living in the dorm. There are som issues regarding the dorm life however, like curfew for undergraduate students(1 am i weekdays), which wasn't that big of an issue as long as you had graduate friends that could let you into the dorm. Visitors was also not allowed into the dorm, which was a bummer as well.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: While the dorms were quite nice and comfortable, and was great for meeting a lot of nice people, i would only stay at the dorm for one semester, as not having your own room, and not being able to have visitors was a bit annoying. But i would defintely recommend it for exchange, as it was very easy and simple to live at the dorm.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: My course registration process was absolutely horrible, and it was the only real problem i encountered on my study abroad. It first began a few weeks before going on exchange, when all of the courses that i wanted to take was unavailable, as the courses that i wanted to take was only available during the spring semester(and i was there in the fall semester). In the course catalog, i could only see the courses for spring while preparing for exchange, which meant that none of the courses i wanted was possible to sign up for. I then only had a few weeks to find new courses that i wanted to take. Besides that, the website itself for finding courses, is very confusing and you have to look through every single major to find available courses. The website was therefore way more confusing and inefficient than it should be.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: When registration was possible, i then found out that they had two phases of registration. There was online registration and offline registration. If i remember correctly, online registration was were you signed up for courses online, were i found out that you could only sign up for courses within your major, which i wasn't aware of beforehand. As the only courses within my major was either in Korean or undergraduate courses, i couldn't apply for any courses in the online registration. In the offline registration, however, i was apply to sign up for some courses that was relevant for my study back home, but it was a very limited amount of courses. I needed to have 3 courses during my study abroad, and i could only find 4 courses that were relevant for my study back home. In the offline registration, it was then required that i asked every single professor for permission to take their course, which was also a challenge. One of the professors said i probably wasn't qualified, but that i could take the course if i wanted to(which meant that most likely wouldn't pass the course). This meant that i now only had 3 courses left that i wanted to take, and i had to get permission for all 3 courses, or i wouldn't be able to complete my exchange abroad. I sent an email to the professors asking for permission to take the course. Only one of them replied, which meant that i had to find the other two professors on campus to ask for their permission. I did manage to find them, and get their permission, but it was indeed a very stressful experience. Once i was registrered in the 3 courses, i then already missed the first week of the course(because it was through offline registration), but that wasn't the big issue. The big issue was the fact that when i turned up to one of my courses, i could see that there was no other exchange students in the entire class, and they all spoke Korean. As the class was about to start, the professor came up to me, and said that i was probably in the wrong class. We then found out that i was signed up for the wrong class, as there was two courses with the same name. One would think i then should able to move to the different course(the one in English), but because it was outside of registration period, i couldn't change course, which was a big problem for me. The professor let me participate in the correct course, and i was able to join the online forum as well, but on paper i was still taking the other class. The administration said that while i couldn't change course, i could take the other course(the one in English), as an auditing student, which meant that my final grades would show that i failed the course i was signed up for(the one in Korean), but that i instead passed another course(the one in English). The administration said that i need permission from my home university in order to do that, which i tried to get. My home university never replied to my mail regarding permission to take a class as an auditing student, which meant that i spend my entire study abroad, not knowing if i would pass 3 courses to complete my exchange, which meant that i was taking a course, that i wasn't signed up for, and i had know idea whether or not i was wasting my time taking this course.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: The administration told me what was possible, and what wasn't possible. While i didn't feel like they were very effective in helping me getting the correct courses, i think it was more or less due to the system and the rules used at the university, which wouldn't allow them to help me any further. I would however like to point out that in the end i passed all 3 courses, and without having to take the course as an auditing student. So while it didn't seem to be possible, it seems like i passed the course without any issues, and it doesn't show that i failed any courses. So one way or another, either the administration or the professor(or maybe both), let me pass the course i signed up for, and i am very grateful to whoever helped with that.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: While it was a very stressful and tedious process, and i didn't know until the end of my echange if i succesfully signed up for all 3 courses, i did manage to get the courses i wanted, which was lucky as i needed these specific courses in order to complete my exchange.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Make sure to find out which courses are available to you when you choose university, and maybe consider applying for another major when on exchange, so that you can sign up for those courses in online registration.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: It was neither too hard or too easy, so i'm satisfied overall.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I had 3 courses, in which two of them was within the "Interaction science" major, and the last one was a business major course. The business major course was "Management information systems", and it was nothing like i expected it to be. The course revolved around the students choosing a research question to work with, and you would then have to work with that research question for the rest of the semester. It was good for me, as i could work with my thesis research question, which helped me find a good research question to write my thesis on, but i didn't really learn anything about management information systems(if i say so myself). The courses in interaction science was nothing like i expected either. The courses were named "Human-AI interaction" and "Service marketing and AI", and i definitely thought i would learn about AI, which wasn't the case. "Service marketing AI" was simply the process of defining a problem, and trying to find solve that problem by developing an app. The solution didn't even have to include AI at all, so that was a bit of a let down. The last course "Human-AI interaction" involved no teaching by the professor himself, which was very weird. Every single week, and selected group of students have to present some kind of AI or system for analyzing data, which was relevant to the AI part of the course, but it was very weird that the course was just presentations during the entire semester.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: While presentations and group projects are very common in the courses i've had at UCPH, i was quite surprised by how each course was very dedicated to one specific kind of teaching. One course was only presentations, another course was only working on a group project, and the last course was me and 4 other students sitting in the professors own office, being targeted to answer questions on the reading material. Overall, i would say the big difference was the lack of teaching by the teachers themselves, as compared to Denmark, you usually get lectures by the professors during class on the reading material. While one course was quite heavy on reading, the other courses involved very limited amount of reading though, which is quite different from my courses at UCPH.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
- Management information systems
- Service marketing AI
- Human-AI interaction

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: The courses within the "Interaction science" major were quite chill, which was nice so that i didn't have to stress that much about school work while on exchange. The course "Management information systems" was however very demanding and tough, but it helped me a lot with preparing for my thesis, so while it was tough, it was definitely the course that i learned the most from.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: Not any to be honest

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Transportation was so very cheap, and buying food at restaurants was also very cheap compared to Denmark. Fruit was however quite expensive, as well as groceries, which is why i never cooked a meal my entire stay in South Korea. When traveling around South Korea, i was surprised how cheap the hotels were, while traveling with flight or bullet train was quite expensive. This is quite different from Europe where housing is expensive, while it's cheap to travel around. Soju was also very cheap, as you could buy an entire bootle of soju for only 11 kr. in a grocery store, which was a very cheap way to get drunk.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I didn't explore that many clubs or activites while on exchange, but i did join the football club, which was a lot of fun. I'll only rate it 4 out of 5, as it would have been nice if i had been told about the different clubs and activites, as i happened to randomly stumble upon the football team.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: I played at the football club at the university, and that was a lot of fun, and they were very welcoming to us foreigners.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Just as i played football on the team, and had a lot of fun with that, i know a lot of exchange students took judo classes, and they really seemed to enjoy that. Doing sports at university was a great way to engage with other koreans, that didn't involve drinking and partying.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: I travelled to Jeju island and Busan, and i would definitely recommend going there. If you go to Jeju, it's best to go there as close to the summer as possible, as it is even better to be there when the weather is great. Going to the Bamboo forest in Busan was definitely cool, and seeing different temples all over South Korea have indeed become memories that i will cherish for the rest of my life.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: If you are just somewhat respectful towards their culture and customs, then it is very easy to adjust to the local culture in South Korea.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: While Koreans are very friendly and helpful, they become way more open and talkative when they are drinking, so that is very good way to socialize with the locals.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Not talking in public transportation was definitely an issue for most exchange students, as people in South Korea will shush you, if you speak too loud(or sometimes if you just speak at all).

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: They are very respectul and kind towards each other, which really helped me enjoy my stay in South Korea. While they didn't have trash cans in the street(which was anoying), the streets were very clean, with just shows how well behaved the locals are. Even as a guy, i also really enjoyed how safe i felt while in South Korea, as there wasn't a single time were i was afraid to get mugged or anything like that. All the female friends i got in South Korea also said that they have never felt as safe walking around alone at night, as they did in South Korea, which is exactly how it should be.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
- Prepare for course registration as much as possible, as it might save you a lot of trouble down the road(only problem i encountered while in South Korea)
- Learn some Korean phrases, as it can both be very helpful to know when you live in Korea, and Koreans become quite happy and friendly when you speak a little korean.
- While it is of course important to fulfill your academic responsibilities, it's not a bad idea to take some easy courses while on exchange. Remember to experience as much of the culture as possible, while also engaging in as many social gatherings and activities as possible, as these will become memories that you will remember for the rest of your life.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: While the fall is pretty warm, it becomes very cold in the winter, so either bring a winterjacket, or buy one when at the university. You also get the possiblity of buying a university baseball jacket, which is both incredibly cool, and hands down the best item i bought while in Korea, but it is also surprisingly warm, and i've been using it during the entire winter period back home in Denmark.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: I learned some Korean phrases when i was still in Denmark, and seeing the Koreans being so happy when you try and speak their language was very rewarding. Even though my Korean was incredibly limited, i could still say some stuff, which was fun.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Course registration.

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: I would definitely recommend going on exchange to South Korea, as it has been an incredible experience. I've created memories that i will cherish forever, and i have created friendships that will spand across the globe, which is very exciting. I'm already meeting friends from all over Europe just 2 months after the exchange has ended, so studying abroad is indeed a great way to get friends from all over the globe.

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
